## Change

Record **18 complete resolutions and four partial results by Matthew J. Colbrook**, Department of Applied Mathematics and Theoretical Physics, University of Cambridge, Cambridge, United Kingdom. All 22 submissions carry his author byline, Cambridge affiliation and email, verified against the [official Cambridge homepage](https://www.damtp.cam.ac.uk/user/mjc249/home.html).

Each complete resolution is marked **Solved** after independent Codex-agent review of its exact catalog target. **IS-05, MI-08, MI-09 and MI-25 remain Partially resolved** with their surviving questions stated explicitly. Original IDs, mathematical statements, references, dated audit history and ratings are preserved; difficulty ratings for complete resolutions are identified as historical.

Please review and merge this contribution into upstream **main**. The branch includes the complete manuscripts, status edits, issue reports, independent reviews and regenerated repository documents.

**MI-03.** The sharp additive contraction constant is $c_k=k/4$ for every $k\ge2$, including every odd summand count. Exact dimension-two extremizers match the universal upper bound. 

**MI-04.** The universal positive-block operator-norm property holds exactly when the off-diagonal block is essentially Hermitian. The proof applies in every finite dimension without invertibility or distinct-singular-value assumptions. 

**MI-06.** No finite constant permits the proposed two-unitary Loewner-order domination for the arithmetic symmetric modulus, already in dimension three. A fixed rational example also refutes the proposed $\sqrt2$ constant. This concerns matrix order, not a separate norm triangle inequality. 

**MI-07.** No finite two-unitary domination constant exists for the maximal symmetric modulus, already in dimension two. The rank-one family gives the necessary bound $C\ge\sqrt{1+t^2}/t$ for every $t>0$. 

**MI-08.** The fixed and adaptive orthogonal pinching lengths both equal the least row count $h(d)$ of a sign matrix $H$ with $H^TH=h(d)I_d$. In particular, the exact length is 12 for $9\le d\le12$. The general value of $h(d)$ is undetermined; the all-dimension optimization remains open and includes Hadamard-order existence questions.

**MI-09.** For every $m\ge2$, the exact dimension-two operator-norm constant is $c_\infty^{\rm sym}(m,2)=\sqrt{6\sqrt3-9}$. This is also the sharp single constant valid simultaneously for every unitarily invariant norm on $M_2$. This does not determine each individual finite Schatten constant. The cases $1<p<\infty$ remain open; the previously established trace endpoint and higher-dimensional operator endpoint are retained.

**MI-19.** A real order-four PSD Gram matrix, $q=7/8$ and the interior singleton $S=\{2\}$ give full minus restricted $q$-permanent equal to $-3235575/16384$. Inversions are counted in the full original ordering. The strict counterexample also persists under sufficiently small positive diagonal perturbations. 

**MI-21.** Two rational positive definite $2\times2$ summands with $s=t=1/2$, $r=2$ and aggregate matrices $A=B=I$ violate the operator-norm inequality for every $p>0$. The left side has eigenvalue $1351000/1350907>1$, while the right side is one. 

**MI-22.** Rational positive definite $3\times3$ matrices at $t=1/8$ violate the first singular-value inequality: the left operator norm exceeds 10900, while $\|AB\|_2<10200$. Exact rational root residuals and a proved operator-root error bound certify the actual principal powers. 

**MI-23.** Rational positive definite $3\times3$ matrices with $r=s=1$, $p=2$ and $t=1/8$ violate the corrected eigenvalue log-majorization conjecture. An exact integer-power construction and rational norm separation establish failure of the first ordered eigenvalue inequality. 

**MI-25.** The trace-norm endpoint has $C_1=\infty$: a real $2\times3$ rank-one family has defect ratio asymptotic to $2/(3t)$ as $t\downarrow0$. Zero-row padding gives the same failure on real $3\times3$ matrices. The remaining finite Schatten exponents $1<p<\infty$ are undetermined by this result; the known value $C_2=1$ is unchanged.

**MI-26.** The real-valued concave function $f(x)=x-x^2$ and two rational projections refute the two-unitary inequality; an explicit positive definite variant also works. The allowed condition is $f(0)\ge0$, without global nonnegativity or monotonicity. This does not refute the narrower nonnegative-valued function class. 

**MI-29.** A rational positive definite $A$ and invertible indefinite Hermitian $B$ in dimension three, with $k=6$ and $p=8$, reverse the proposed determinant comparison. The exact right-minus-left gap is $21036678407451/156250000000000>0$. The known $k=2$ theorem and the variant $B>0$ are not contradicted.

| [IS-05](https://github.com/ajt60gaibb/OpenProblemsInNLA/issues/11) | Partially resolved | [Theorems 1–2 and equations (4)–(8)](https://github.com/MColbrook/OpenProblemsInNLA/blob/cca7173f77342df755800fa50836d55f30ba4b0a/eigenvalues-and-inverse-problems/IS-05/solution.md) | [PASS (partial only)](https://github.com/MColbrook/OpenProblemsInNLA/blob/cca7173f77342df755800fa50836d55f30ba4b0a/references/colbrook-additional-2026-09-11/verification/reviews/IS-05-review.md) | Partial only: $17/92\le\alpha_*\le1/2$, with the exact exponent still open. |

The surviving IS-05 exponent question has the partial interval $17/92\le\alpha_*\le1/2$. The exact exponent remains open. KE-03 concerns exact matrix-vector query complexity, not total bit complexity; IE-08 uses the stated floating-point oracle and precision model.

### Verification level and reproducibility

Nine separate Codex review agents covered the 22 arguments, with one independent report per argument. The original drafts were AI-assisted. All complete arguments passed against their exact targets; the four partial verdicts apply only to their explicitly limited results. This is independent agent verification, not external human peer review or formal proof certification. No exhaustive novelty or priority claim is made.

The dated submission records retain original manuscripts, normalized full-file hashes, detailed reviews and supporting diagnostics: [first five](https://github.com/MColbrook/OpenProblemsInNLA/blob/cca7173f77342df755800fa50836d55f30ba4b0a/references/colbrook-2026-09-11/README.md), [three further resolutions and IS-05](https://github.com/MColbrook/OpenProblemsInNLA/blob/cca7173f77342df755800fa50836d55f30ba4b0a/references/colbrook-additional-2026-09-11/README.md), and [thirteen matrix results](https://github.com/MColbrook/OpenProblemsInNLA/blob/cca7173f77342df755800fa50836d55f30ba4b0a/references/colbrook-matrix-2026-09-11/README.md). Matrix proof sections are embedded unchanged in standalone authored TeX, with an inline bibliography. Exact diagnostic checks pass; the independent reviews separately cover analytic arguments that those checks cannot establish.

## Documents checked

- All 22 affected canonical Markdown, standalone TeX and PDF documents, authored manuscripts, category indexes, CATALOG.md, README counts and RESOLVED.md are updated. The final catalog contains **202 entries: 100 Open, 82 Partially resolved, 19 Solved, one Solution claimed**; the open count is **182**.
- The 26 PDFs for the thirteen matrix results were compiled, rasterized and visually inspected on every page. Author metadata, relative links, theorem locators, original-target preservation and all thirteen embedded proof hashes were checked. XeLaTeX reports no overfull boxes, missing characters or unresolved references. Earlier authored and canonical outputs passed their documented checks.
- Supplied rational diagnostics and separately written independent rational checkers pass. Original review inputs are archived; the independent scripts were routed to those identical archived files for public reproducibility.
- `tools/update_catalog.py` is idempotent. Diff whitespace checks pass with intentional Markdown line-break spaces allowed. The native TeX submission renderer preserves reviewed proof text and produces independently compilable exports; BibTeX is required for regeneration of these manuscripts.

Related issue reports are linked in the tables. Upstream acceptance is pending; these branch status changes do not imply the PR has been merged.

items.body:
The [complete proof](https://github.com/sgstepaniants/OpenProblemsInNLA/blob/dcd362b46b0c20a9ca5f38c9ab35138c452a65ee/randomized-and-low-rank-approximation/KE-05/solution.md) disproves KE-05's spectrum-uniform probability bound. At fixed `b=2, d=3`, deterministic admissible diagonal blocks make the normalized transformed block diverge while the coefficient factor stays bounded below. Consequently, the product tends to infinity in probability, contradicting a uniform bound already at failure probability `1/2`.

Closes #142.

George Stepaniants is the author, with Department of Computing and Mathematical Sciences, California Institute of Technology affiliation. Shao retains credit for the conjecture and framework. Substantial AI assistance is disclosed. A separate [independent Codex-agent audit](https://github.com/sgstepaniants/OpenProblemsInNLA/blob/dcd362b46b0c20a9ca5f38c9ab35138c452a65ee/references/stepaniants-ke05-2026-09-12/independent-review.md) passed the complete proof and exact canonical target. This is informal review, not external human peer review or formal verification.

The original recurrence, hypotheses, probability quantifiers, statement, references and history remain unchanged. The example uses permitted interlaced block spectra and within-block repetition; it makes no claim about a separate ordered-interval variant or block Lanczos output convergence.

The package adds standalone proof Markdown/TeX/PDF, the retained canonical documents, a named RESOLVED entry, regenerated indexes, and a reproducible review/source/verification record. All 98 proof formulas and 29 canonical formulas match TeX in order; the mathematical core is byte-identical to the reviewed source. The five-page proof and two-page canonical PDFs compile with XeLaTeX and every final page was inspected. A KE-05-only renderer adjustment removes an unnecessary reference-page break.

Validation passes: both published-base ID checks; 17 ID tests and three status tests; 46 drafting-agent exact checks and the reviewer's independent polynomial and reordered-instance checks; source/target preservation; local links; author/affiliation and no-contact-email checks. The final public-network audit found no competing resolution across six repositories and 47 public heads. See the [immutable submission record](https://github.com/sgstepaniants/OpenProblemsInNLA/blob/dcd362b46b0c20a9ca5f38c9ab35138c452a65ee/references/stepaniants-ke05-2026-09-12/README.md) for exact scope and reproduction commands.

Please review this new negative resolution for inclusion in `main` when the mathematical and repository checks are satisfactory.
